title: BUG: HDFStore.append silently reinterpreted stored rows when tz-naive and tz-aware data met
body:
No GitHub issue; found while reviewing the pytables append path.

`IndexCol.update_info` raises on a `tz` conflict only when both sides are non-`None`, so an incoming `None` instead falls through to the assignment arm and overwrites the stored `tz`. Appending tz-naive data to a tz-aware table key (or the reverse) was accepted with no warning, and the rows already on disk then read back as different instants — one stored `tz` governs how the whole column is localized on read.

This adds a `_check_tz_conflict` guard raising `TypeError` for the `None` cases, on both the index axis and data columns (so it also covers `data_columns`, MultiIndex levels and `Series` values). Two different concrete timezones already raised and are unchanged. Same shape as the `freq` guard in GH-68523.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5 (high)`), which reproduced the bug, wrote the fix and tests, and ran the pytables suite.

title: BUG: SparseDtype equality ignored a non-default fill_value (GH#68582)
body:
Once either side's ``fill_value`` was NA, ``SparseDtype.__eq__`` compared fill values by Python *type* rather than value, so an NA fill matched every fill of that type: ``Sparse[float64, nan] == Sparse[float64, 1.5]`` was ``True``. Two consequences beyond the equality itself: those pairs compared equal while hashing differently, breaking the hash/eq invariant; and `SparseArray.astype` short-circuits on `dtype == self._dtype`, so `astype` to such a dtype silently returned the original array.

The fix requires both sides to be NA before the type check, which still lets the `float("nan")`/`np.nan` and `pd.NaT`/`np.datetime64("NaT")` spellings compare equal while keeping a NaN distinct from a NaT.

Three existing sparse tests were asserting behavior the loose equality had masked, and are corrected here: `test_where_series` hardcoded a `0.0` fill where `where` actually keeps the array's own fill value, `test_fillna_no_op_returns_copy` expected `fillna` not to move the fill value on an NA-filled array (it does, per its docstring), and `test_arith_frame_with_scalar` `truediv`/`rtruediv` join the existing "result dtype.fill_value mismatch" xfail, since the vectorized result correctly keeps the `0.0` fill that the `Series.combine` reference loses.

Overlaps with GH-68567, which fixes the same `__eq__` defect and additionally covers `concat`, `select_dtypes`, and the `Series`/`DataFrame.astype` short-circuits. Opened separately rather than folded in; one of the two should be closed once you pick. Filed as a draft for that reason.

title: BUG: SparseArray.sum mishandled a non-missing object fill_value
body:
`SparseArray.sum` computes `sp_sum + self.fill_value * nsparse`, where `sp_sum` is the sum of the stored values and `nsparse` the number of gaps. That closed form assumes addition is commutative, which str and bytes concatenation is not:

- `SparseArray(["a", "a", "b"], fill_value="a").sum()` returned `'baa'` where the dense `pd.Series(["a", "a", "b"]).sum()` returns `'aab'` — the gaps were appended instead of taking their actual positions.
- When no stored value was non-NA, the expression degenerated to `int(0) + str` and raised `TypeError`. That includes a column entirely equal to its fill value, e.g. `SparseArray(["a", "a"], fill_value="a").sum()`.

Object subtypes with a non-missing fill value now reduce on the dense values through `_dense_reduce`, the in-file helper `SparseArray.prod` already uses. A missing fill value deliberately keeps the closed form: its gaps are skipped rather than added, so it needs no adjustment and already returns the stored order.

title: BUG: SparseArray.shift raised for a boolean or datetimelike subtype
body:
Noticed while looking at sparse fill-value handling; no existing issue.

`SparseArray.shift` decided its result subtype with `np.result_type(fill_value, self.dtype.subtype)`, which is neither value-aware nor dtype-safe:

- a boolean subtype with the default fill raised `ValueError: fill_value must be a valid value for the SparseDtype.subtype`, because `np.result_type(nan, bool)` is `float64` and `SparseDtype(float64, False)` fails validation;
- every datetimelike subtype raised `numpy.exceptions.DTypePromotionError` with the default fill, and `TypeError: Cannot interpret 'Timestamp(...)' as a data type` with an explicit `Timestamp`/`Timedelta` fill, since `np.result_type` was being handed a *value* where it wants a dtype;
- for other subtypes the result dtype disagreed with `Series.shift` in both directions — `fill_value=True` on an `int64` subtype was stored as `1`, and `fill_value=2.0` widened `int64` to `float64` where dense keeps `int64`.

Dense `Series.shift` handles all of these. The fix routes that one line through `_promote_for_fill`, the helper in the same module that `take`/`_take_with_fill` already use for exactly this computation (added in GH-68469).

Pre-existing rather than a recent regression: the `np.result_type` line dates to 823adcfff88 (GH-23947).

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5 (high)`), which wrote the fix and tests and ran a multi-round review of the branch; reviewed by me before opening.

title: BUG: sparse comparisons densified a masked operand and lost its NA

labels.name: NA - MaskedArrays
labels.description: Related to pd.NA and nullable extension arrays

body:
`SparseArray._cmp_method` called `np.asarray(other)` on an ExtensionArray operand, which turns a
masked array's `pd.NA` into an object `pd.NA` that the sparse kernels cannot evaluate:

```python
mb = pd.array([True, pd.NA, True, False], dtype="boolean")
SparseArray(np.array([True, False, True, False])) == mb
# AttributeError: module 'pandas._libs.sparse' has no attribute 'sparse_eq_object'

mi = pd.array([1, pd.NA, 3, 0], dtype="Int64")
SparseArray(np.array([1, 0, 3, 0])) < mi
# Sparse[bool] [False, False, False, False]   <- dense gives [False, <NA>, False, False]
```

The `<` case is the sharp one: a silently wrong `False` in the NA slot rather than an error.

`_cmp_method` now returns `NotImplemented` for a `BaseMaskedDtype` operand, so the masked
operand's reflected comparison runs and keeps its NA semantics. This is the gate GH-68483 added
to `_logical_method`, here covering every masked dtype rather than only boolean -- masked
`_cmp_method` consumes arbitrary list-likes, so the non-boolean masked dtypes work in the
reflected direction too.

The scalar arm had the same defect: `SparseArray(...) == pd.NA` and `& pd.NA` raised
`TypeError: boolean value of NA is ambiguous`, because the arm assigns an object result into a
`np.bool_` array. It now answers `pd.NA` the way the dense path does -- all-`False`, all-`True`
for `!=`, and `ops.invalid_comparison` for a datetimelike subtype, which refuses to be ordered
against NA as the dense arrays do.

The shared body of `_cmp_method` is split out as `_cmp_or_logical_op`, which `_logical_method`'s
fast path calls ungated so the logical ops keep their existing operand handling. The `pd.NA` arm
lives in that shared body, so `Sp[bool] & pd.NA` is fixed alongside the comparisons.

tests and ran a multi-round blind self-review over the diff.

title: BUG: SparseArray mishandled a boxed Timestamp/Timedelta fill value
body:
closes #68571

Supersedes GH-68571, which fixed the `__array__` half of this; that PR's fix and tests are included here unchanged, plus the items below.

A datetime64/timedelta64 `SparseArray` whose `fill_value` is a boxed `pd.Timestamp`/`pd.Timedelta`, rather than the `np.datetime64`/`np.timedelta64` spelling of the same value, was mishandled wherever the fill value reached numpy:

- `np.result_type(sp_values.dtype, type(fill_value))` gives `object` for a boxed pandas scalar, so `np.asarray` and `astype(object)` returned `object` dtype holding the stored values unboxed — raw `int64` on a nanosecond unit, `datetime.datetime` on a coarser one.
- `np.full` and `np.insert` route a boxed pandas scalar through the stdlib datetime protocol, which truncates to microseconds, so `to_dense()`, `unique()` and `value_counts()` materialized a sub-microsecond `fill_value` as a *different* value.

`SparseArray._densify` already guarded the second case with `fill_value.asm8`. This extracts that into a `_unbox_fill_value` helper and wires it into `__array__`, `unique`, `value_counts` and the existing `_promote_for_fill`. The helper is guarded on the subtype itself being datetimelike — an object subtype has to keep the boxed scalar, or it loses the nanosecond or the timezone.

The `fill_value is NaT` special case in `__array__` is removed as dead: GH-68449 made `SparseDtype.__init__` normalize a `pd.NaT` fill to the subtype's own NaT, and every route to a `SparseArray`'s fill value goes through that constructor.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5 (high)`), which wrote the fix, the tests and this description; reviewed and verified by me.

title: BUG: date and tz-aware Timestamp mix raised "Mixed timezones detected"

labels.name: Index
labels.description: Related to the Index class or subclasses

body:
`Index._maybe_downcast_for_indexing`'s `datetime.date` branch converts an object-dtype date Index to the other side's `DatetimeIndex` so the two can be compared, and caught only `OutOfBoundsDatetime`. When the object Index mixed `datetime.date` objects with timezone-aware `Timestamp`s, that conversion escaped instead:

```python
from datetime import date
import pandas as pd

left = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([[date(2001, 1, 1)], ["foo"]])
right = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
    [pd.DatetimeIndex([pd.Timestamp("2001-01-01", tz="UTC")]), ["bar"]]
)
left.union(right)
# ValueError: Mixed timezones detected. Pass utc=True in to_datetime or
#   tz='UTC' in DatetimeIndex to convert to a common timezone.
```

That message names `to_datetime` from inside a set operation, and its suggested remedy raises the same error. The naive equivalent of this call works — GH-66136 fixed that case — and flat `Index.union` already returned an object-dtype result.

`OutOfBoundsDatetime` is a `ValueError` subclass, so widening the clause covers both and falls back to leaving the index as object dtype, which is what the GH-62158 deprecation a few lines below says will happen unconditionally in 4.0.

Also affected and fixed, all measured before and after: `MultiIndex.append` and `symmetric_difference`, `Index.get_indexer`, `get_indexer_non_unique`, `join` and `difference`, and `Series.reindex` / `DataFrame.reindex`. `.loc[[date, aware_ts]]` changes from the `ValueError` to the `KeyError` it should have raised.

Found while auditing GH-66136.

title: BUG: Timedelta times a bool array did not raise (GH#62316)
body:
`pd.Timedelta("1D") * np.array([True, False])` returned `[1 days, 0 days]` instead of raising, while every other spelling of the same multiplication already raised `TypeError`: the bool scalar forms (`True`, `np.bool_(True)`, a 0-d bool array) via GH-62316, and `timedelta64`-dtype containers times a bool array via GH-58054. Bool-dtype `Series`, `Index` and `BooleanArray` operands leaked through the same hole, since `Timedelta` returns `NotImplemented` for those and the operation is then re-evaluated as `bool_ndarray * Timedelta`.

`Timedelta.__mul__` handles arrays before it handles bools: the `is_array` arm falls through to `other * self.to_timedelta64()` for any dtype outside `"iuf"`, so numpy performed the multiplication. This gives that arm the `kind == "b"` rejection the `TimedeltaArray` path already applies.

title: BUG: slice and other subscript keys raised in query/eval expressions (GH#49905)
body:
closes #49905

`visit_Slice` read `.value` off each visited bound, but only a `Constant` term has one, so a negative or computed bound raised `AttributeError: 'UnaryOp' object has no attribute 'value'`. `visit_Subscript` then re-evaluated the already-visited key by passing it back through `pd_eval`, which stringifies a slice into a `slice(...)` call — not a supported function — so even a constant-bound slice raised `ValueError: "slice" is not a supported function`. Between them no slice subscript has ever worked in `query`/`eval`; `visit_Slice` has been unreachable-in-practice since it was added in 2013.

The subscript key is now resolved without the round trip: a bare `slice` passes through, an already-resolved `Term` uses its value, and an `Op` still goes to `pd_eval` so the engine keeps evaluating and aligning it.

A tuple key such as `arr[1, 2]` now raises `NotImplementedError`: `visit_Tuple` builds a list, which would select along axis 0 rather than across axes. No tuple spelling has ever evaluated correctly; making them work is a separate change.

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({"a": ["bc"]})
df.query("a.str[-1:] == 'c'")   # was AttributeError, now selects the row
df.query("a.str[1:] == 'c'")    # was ValueError: "slice" is not a supported function
```

The issue’s original report (`a.str.slice(0, -1)`) was already fixed; the `a.str[-1:]` spelling in its comment thread is what this repairs.

title: BUG: sparse to dense astype rounded uint64 and mangled a boxed datetimelike fill value
body:
The dense-target branch of `SparseArray.astype` densified with `np.asarray(self)`, and `SparseArray.__array__` picks its output dtype from `np.result_type(self.sp_values.dtype, type(self.fill_value))` — the fill value's *class*, not its value. Two consequences:

- a `uint64` subtype with a Python `int` fill value promoted to `float64`, silently rounding values above `2**53`;
- a `datetime64`/`timedelta64` subtype with a boxed `Timestamp`/`Timedelta` fill value made `np.result_type` raise, so `__array__` fell back to `object` holding the stored values as raw `int64` — which cast to a garbage date for a unit change, raised `TypeError` for an integer target, and gave mixed boxed/raw values for `object`.

```python
big = 2**63 + 12345
ser = pd.Series(np.array([1, 0, big], dtype="uint64")).astype(pd.SparseDtype("uint64", 0))
ser.astype("uint64").to_numpy()
# before: [1, 0, 9223372036854788096]   <- off by 57
# after:  [1, 0, 9223372036854788153]
```

`_densify()` was added in GH-66690 for exactly this promotion problem but was never wired into `astype`; this routes the densification through it. `_densify()` did not propagate the read-only flag that `__array__` did, so that is restored there too — otherwise `astype` hands back a writeable alias of an immutable `Index`.

Also corrects `astype`'s docstring, which still documented the pre-GH-34457 contract (`Returns: SparseArray`, "output will always be a SparseArray") and recommended `numpy.asarray`, the path this fixes `astype` to avoid.

`np.asarray`/`to_numpy` on a sparse array are still affected by the underlying `__array__` promotion; that is a wider blast radius and wants its own PR.
